review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Mathematical written forms, fraction and decimal representations, numerical ratios and percentages, equation/proportion notation, and calculation targets.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet. CC BY 4.0 and the underlying Princeton notice are retained in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. OpenStax sources are credited individually; the notation/value distinctions and graph mappings are adaptations.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and assertions use U1. Existing home contexts and U3 programming meanings are preserved. Information object 265 gains its established abstract-object genus in U1 as well as U3. U2 stays empty.
review.representation_policy: Written expressions and numerals are information objects, distinct from the abstract numbers they denote. A fraction source synset classified by value is explicitly adapted to its written-form sense; numeral-to-number denotation is not encoded as is-a, container content, causal production or equality of class extensions.

sense_decisions.scope: An individual written mathematical form; not the entire notational system or the physical ink. This is an explicit written-form adaptation of the dictionary notation-system sense.
A symbol used in mathematical notation. Its meaning is distinct from its printed glyph or a programming character.
A written expression, including a numeral, variable symbol, or valid combination of operation symbols. It need not assert a proposition; do not copy the dictionary mathematical-statement genus.
A mathematical expression using number representations and operation signs, with no free variable required. A formula and its evaluated number are distinct.
A symbol or written form representing a number, not the number itself and not a grammatical numeral word.
Select a numeral symbol used as an element of a numeration system, not its integer value, a finger or a length measure. The OEWN integer genus is not copied.
One of the ten decimal digit symbols. This does not assert that every digit in every numeral system is decimal.
A numerator-over-denominator expression, evaluated only where the denominator is nonzero. The general expression may have symbolic components; its value is separate.
A fractional representation with integer numerator and nonzero integer denominator. Values such as 5/5 may be integers; do not equate the notation with non-integer values.
A common fraction whose absolute value is less than one. For nonnegative fractions with positive denominator this is numerator < denominator.
A common fraction whose absolute value is at least one. Include equal numerator/denominator magnitudes, such as 5/5; OEWN omits this boundary.
A common fraction in lowest terms: numerator and denominator have no common positive integer factor greater than one. This is independent of being proper or improper.
A whole-number part written together with a proper fractional part. This is the written form, not a new number class; the sign of a negative mixed numeral applies to the whole magnitude.
A positional base-ten representation. This selected form is distinct from the abstract real number and from the whole decimal notation system.
A finite decimal representation. The finite written form is distinct from another recurring representation of the same value.
An infinite decimal representation whose digit sequence eventually repeats. Do not make it a child of the finite power-of-ten-denominator fraction gloss.
The expression above the fraction bar, representing the dividend. The general numerator can be an algebraic expression; do not classify every such expression as an integer.
The expression below the fraction bar, representing the divisor. Evaluation excludes values for which it is zero.
A shared denominator representation for numerical fractions; the represented integer is a common multiple of the original denominators. Exclude the figurative common-attribute sense.
The shared denominator form representing the least positive common multiple of the numerical denominators. It is not the greatest common divisor.
The division-separating mark in fraction notation, whether horizontal or an appropriate slanted fraction stroke. Do not import the filesystem slash meaning.
The percent mark in a written percentage, distinct from the numeric ratio and its per-hundred scaling.
A written percentage with its percent sign. It denotes a per-hundred ratio; the sign is part of the notation, not part of the abstract number.
The quotient value comparing two numbers, with a nonzero second operand. This is the numerical result sense, not all quantitative relations and not ratio notation itself.
The quotient comparing a nonnegative part with its positive whole, within zero and one. Distinct from the existing part/share object 2903.
A numerical ratio expressed per hundred. It may exceed 100 percent; do not classify all percentages as a bounded part-to-whole share.
A written equality joining two mathematical expressions. It can be true or false and is distinct from equality as a relation and from the act of equating.
An equation in which values of an unknown are to be determined. The narrower Russian equation usage is recorded separately from a purely numerical equality.
A mathematical equality of two ratios, distinct from a single part-to-whole quotient or harmonious shape.
A symbol standing for a varying or unspecified value in a mathematical expression. Preserve the separate U3 programming-variable object.
A number with a fixed value in the selected mathematical context, separate from a programming constant declaration.
The fixed numerical factor of a term, with the mathematical context held fixed. Symbolic coefficient functions are outside this selected numeric sense.
The number being divided. Exclude financial dividend and do not identify the value with a written numerator expression.
The numerical operand by which another number is divided. This selected sense does not require exact integer divisibility.
Calculate the value of a mathematical expression where it is defined. This is a process, distinct from an abstract arithmetic function.
Determine the numerical comparison quotient; no division-by-zero value is asserted.
Determine a numerical ratio expressed per hundred, allowing values greater than one hundred percent.
A process changing the written mathematical form. General transformations need not preserve value unless their narrower definition says so.
Divide numerator and denominator by a shared nonzero integer factor to obtain an equivalent fraction. Cancellation concerns factors, not arbitrary added terms.
Rewrite numerical fractions with a shared denominator while preserving each represented value.
Evaluate a fraction expression only where its denominator is nonzero.
Retain the U3 language-construct sense; it is not merged into mathematical notation.
Keep the programming syntax role separate from a numeric division operand.
Keep the U3 programming object separate from a mathematical symbol.
Keep the programming declaration meaning separate from a fixed numerical value.
Its existing speech/utterance ancestry selects verbal expression, not a mathematical expression.
The relation remains distinct from a written equation.
Reuse the existing number obtained by division as the nearest numerical-ratio genus.
Reuse the existing part/share object and keep it distinct from a numerical part-to-whole ratio.
Reuse information object with an explicit U1 genus.
Reuse calculation as the action genus.
Reuse change for expression transformations.
Reuse sign without importing mathematical statements as speech acts.
Reuse symbol as the mathematical-symbol genus.
Keep the general symbolic formula separate; mathematical/chemical subtypes remain for future review.
Reuse the abstract number anchor; notation is not its subtype.
Reuse integer as the numerical operand domain in source review, without classifying numeral syntax as integer.
Reuse rational number; fraction representations are not new distinct rational values.

The adjective fractional and legacy number genus do not specify whether this is a property, non-integer value, or fraction representation. Preserve it pending a dedicated lexical decision; do not merge it into the new written fraction.
Logical identity remains separate from equation notation and an algebraic identity valid for all admissible values.

The dictionary decimal-fraction gloss is restricted to a proper fraction with power-of-ten denominator, while its repeating-decimal child exceeds that definition. Use separate representation genera; do not import the conflicting hierarchy.

review.limits: The old fractional record 4824 remains pending because the adjective and numeric genus do not identify a precise value sense. General formula 2658, speech expression 2842, logical identity 5024 and numeric/programming homonyms are not merged. No arithmetic engine, literal value records, conversion coefficients or equation solver is added. Nonzero denominators and equality cases are review constraints, not executable arithmetic predicates. No application test suites.

collision_decisions.math_expression: Keep the mathematical written form distinct from programming 428 and verbal 2842.
collision_decisions.math_variable: Keep the mathematical symbol distinct from programming variable 436 and Var construct 1179.
collision_decisions.part_whole_ratio: Keep the numerical comparison distinct from share/part object 2903.

review.previous_conditions: All Q12 conditions remain required without exceptions. The retained Q11 conditions remain unchanged, with only the four direct genera already superseded in Q12.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: String candidates only. No exact English match does not establish a missing meaning.
